topo_description: Topography determines where water moves, where soil erodes, and where microclimates form. Even subtle grade changes on a small parcel shape what can grow and what drains.
flood_zone_description: Zone X is FEMA's designation for areas of minimal flood hazard, outside the 0.2% annual chance floodplain.
hydro_description: Your parcel drains into a local watershed that feeds the Neuse River basin. Understanding flow direction and flood risk is the foundation of responsible water management.
climate_description: Thirty-year climate normals establish the baseline your landscape operates within. Seasonal precipitation and temperature patterns determine what thrives here without intervention.

soils_description: Soil determines drainage, infiltration, and what can root deeply enough to persist. SSURGO data identifies the map units under this parcel and their behavior.
micro_description: Microclimate varies across even a small property. Aspect, canopy cover, and building proximity create zones of heat accumulation and cooling that determine plant stress and comfort.
vulnerabilities: The steepest ground (4% of the parcel above 15% grade) sits where runoff concentrates.
The dominant map unit (CeB2) is classified as moderately eroded.
opportunities: The flat front section (65% of the parcel under 2% grade) suits infiltration-based stormwater handling.
Zone X flood status leaves siting unconstrained by floodplain rules.
synthesis_narrative: This section contains the practitioner's professional synthesis — observations from the site visit combined with the data findings above. It identifies vulnerabilities the data revealed and opportunities the site offers for ecologically grounded design.
